name: Skirmishers of Exodus

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

short: The main reason for the mass exodus of tribes during the Migration period was the invasion of nomads, the warlike and bloodthirsty Huns, and partly due to dramatic changes in the climate. Thousands and thousands of barbarians left their settled homes in search of a better life in new places. The newcomers were impressive not only in numbers: though many of them were women and children, the barbarians moved with their families, with carts, goods, horses, - but their backbone was composed of hard healthy warriors. They had no way back, and they would have to take every step into a new life with weapons in their hands.
history: Rome liked to have the best of everything. When it came to skirmishers 'funditores', Latin for 'slingers', were recruited to accompany its Legions on campaign as early as the Punic Wars of the 3rd century BC. The best slingers in the western Mediterranean came from the Balearic islands, where it is said that children had to 'sling for their dinners' - having to knock their bread from a wall at range before being permitted to eat by their parents. In the eastern Mediterranean, the rocky crags of islands such as Crete produced fine skirmishers, be they slingers, javelineers or archers. During Imperial Rome's almost constant wars against the eastern empires local skirmishers were drafted into fight, honouring the long-standing traditions of their inhospitable homelands and enabling the Romans to 'level the playing field' in terms of army structure and tactics.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
